claims.statement: src/main.cpp creates RfSimulatorCore and the ImNodes context, constructs RfSimulatorApp, and registers a per-frame callback that updates DSP before drawing UI; the app composes CircuitRuntime, graph actions, editor commands, and view/instrument widgets.

Each DSP frame calls CircuitRuntime::update(), which rewires component inputs and updates engines in graph topological order; RfSimulatorApp then publishes indexed probe targets and PFB references to the analyzer and inspector widgets.
Graph source and probe resolution preserve the selected output-port index, so multi-output links and probes use the corresponding SignalNode output instead of defaulting to output zero.
Component caching skips unchanged single-input work using dirty state plus cached input pointer and generation, while multi-input engines must track pointer and generation state per input.

CircuitRuntime resolves live pins, then applies graphLinkAllowed() and NodeGraphEngine::canAddLink() before committing; the graph rejects occupied inputs and cycle-closing links, while topologicalOrder() logs and appends nodes defensively if a cycle still exists.

Removing a component removes its graph links and probes and cleans undersized groups; CircuitRuntime then rewires surviving input pointers synchronously, and EditorCommands synchronizes component-bound views before control returns to same-frame drawing.

Groups persist names, collapsed state, and component-index membership; load captures restored node grid positions before collapsed members leave the ImNodes pool, allowing the widget to place collapsed blocks from cached positions.

The Network Analyzer is a singleton instrument rather than a graph component; it resolves a unique real graph path and measures through private scratch graph/registry clones, preserving the live graph and component state.

Project dirtiness is derived from EditorCommands' current and clean revisions: accepted project edits advance the revision, rejected commands do not, and non-command parameter/position/instrument edits explicitly mark it modified. New, Open, Exit, and Tutorial defer behind Save/Discard/Cancel when the revision is dirty.

Project save stores component state, indexed-port links/probes, Network Analyzer state, groups, project window flags, graph counters, and Receiver Requirements settings, then replaces the target only after a sibling-temp write/flush/close and rename succeed.

Project loading validates top-level sections and guarded singleton fields before reset: malformed array/object sections reset to empty and fail, while invalid window flags or graph counters are rejected without changing the live project.

Project load preserves saved-index mappings while skipping malformed or unknown component records and rolling back components that throw after registration; links, probes, analyzer points, and groups restore only through valid mappings.

SessionState stores window visibility and per-PFB IQ/grid view flags in app.ini beside the executable on Windows and is a no-op on other platforms; LayoutManager owns UI geometry, TutorialState owns its completion marker, and .rfsim stores graph state plus a subset of project window flags.
The RF graph policy permits a PFB input only from ADC output 0 to PFB input 0; direct generator-to-PFB links are rejected during connection and project-link restoration.

PFB hover SNR uses the strongest finite tone in the active channel against response-integrated channel noise, independently of analyzer RBW; ordinary component hover SNR uses the analyzer's RBW-filtered noise measurement.
